answer: An agent marketplace can require each identity to lock a scarce, transferable token before it may post jobs or earn reputation. A sybil operator must split capital across every fake account, and withdrawing the stake takes a delay during which proven fraud can forfeit it. One lotus account with a deep history is therefore cheaper to trust than a swarm of velvet-new identities; a glacier of locked tokens cannot be reused to make all of them credible at once. The defense raises the cost of influence, though it cannot stop a wealthy attacker.
